newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jobs focus in German insurance sector wage round.
newsitem.headline: Jobs focus in German insurance sector wage round.

text.p: Trade union officials said on Wednesday job protection measures were a "high priority" for them at the start of wage talks for the 240,000-plus workers in the German insurance sector.
They said they were demanding such measures because of plans by insurance companies to cut staff levels despite expectations of higher premium income and profits in 1997.
Banking and insurance trade union HBV said some 20,000 jobs had already been lost in the sector over the last five years.

HBV and the white-collar trade union DAG, also involved in the negotiations, have not named a precise 1997 wage demand but have said they are seeking a general package significantly above the current inflation rate.
A DAG spokesman said earlier it expected "difficult" negotiations.
